To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
displacement-based WI provides accurate results for linear elastic and nonlinear vessels but it deviated from the pressure-based WI when the wall is viscoelastic.
the accuracy of displacement based WIA depends on the material properties of the vessel wall.
the agreement between displacement-based WI and pressure-based WI is excellent for large arteries with linear elastic walls and is good for vessels with nonlinear and/or viscoelastic walls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of displacement based WI and its application in clinical practice.
the accuracy of WIA when the displacement is utilized instead of pressure.
the accuracy of the wall displacement-based WI for different vascular models and its agreement with pressure-based WI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the displacement-based WI analysis is accurate for vessels with linear and nonlinear elastic walls, but it can be inaccurate for vessels with viscoelastic walls.
displacement-based wave intensity is accurate for large vessels that have linear elastic wall and no irregularities.
displacement-based WI provides a reliable alternative to pressure-based WI for the assessment of local and global cardiovascular hemodynamics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
displacement-based WIA can be used in clinical practice for large central arteries, such as aorta and carotid artery, where the vessel wall is elastic.
for vessels that are not viscoelastic and do not have irregular geometry, the displacement-based WIA is as accurate as the pressure-based WIA.
displacement-based WI can be a clinically useful alternative to pressure-based WI in large central arteries with linear elastic walls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of displacement-derived WIA is highly dependent on the material properties of the vessel wall.
the displacement-based WI should not be used for vessels with viscoelastic properties.
displacement-based WI can be used as an alternative method for pressure-based WI.
